get_workflow_versions_diff.description: Compare two saved versions of a workflow and return what changed between them: nodes added (with their full content), removed, or modified (with a field-level delta per modified node) and connections added or removed. Pass the older version as fromVersionId and the newer one as toVersionId, using version IDs from get_workflow_history.

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow the versions belong to

fromVersionId.description: The base (older) version ID, as returned by get_workflow_history

toVersionId.description: The target (newer) version ID, as returned by get_workflow_history

get_workflow_versions_diff.name: get_workflow_versions_diff

nodesAdded.description: Full content of nodes present in the target version but not in the base version (credentials reduced to { id, name }), so the diff is self-contained

id.description: The credential ID, used to reference this credential in write operations

name.description: The credential name

additionalProperties.description: The credential assigned to this slot (id and name only, never secret data)

credentials.description: Credentials assigned to the node, keyed by credential type (e.g. "slackApi"). Reuse these when adding nodes for the same service to this workflow.

nodesRemoved.description: Nodes present in the base version but not in the target version. Fetch the base version with get_workflow_version if you need their content.

nodesModified.description: Nodes present in both versions whose content changed (position-only moves are not reported). Listed by their name in the target version.

changes.description: Field-level delta in json-diff format: changed values appear as { __old, __new }, added keys as "<key>__added", removed keys as "<key>__deleted", array changes as [op, value] tuples.

connectionsAdded.description: Connections present in the target version but not the base version. Renaming a node does not by itself produce connection changes; endpoints are matched by node id.

from.description: Source node name, using its target-version name, or its base-version name if the node no longer exists there

to.description: Target node name, using its target-version name, or its base-version name if the node no longer exists there

fromOutput.description: Index of the source node output (e.g. 0 = true branch, 1 = false branch on an If)

toInput.description: Index of the target node input (e.g. 1 = second input of a Merge)

connectionsRemoved.description: Connections present in the base version but not the target version.

from.description: Source node name, using its target-version name, or its base-version name if the node no longer exists there

to.description: Target node name, using its target-version name, or its base-version name if the node no longer exists there

fromOutput.description: Index of the source node output (e.g. 0 = true branch, 1 = false branch on an If)

toInput.description: Index of the target node input (e.g. 1 = second input of a Merge)

publish_agent.description: Publish a valid Agent draft and activate its tasks and integrations. Pass versionId to republish a previously published version instead. Only call after the user explicitly requests or confirms publication; completing a build does not imply approval.

versionId.description: Republish a previously published version instead of the current draft. The draft is left untouched.

publish_agent.name: publish_agent

create_workflow_from_code.description: Create a workflow in n8n from validated SDK code. This tool expects code that already follows the n8n Workflow SDK patterns and has passed validate_workflow. If code fails to parse, call get_workflow_sdk_reference, rewrite the code using the reference, validate again, then retry creation. If the user named a target project, resolve it via search_projects before calling this tool; when projectId is omitted, the workflow is created in the user's personal project. If the user named a target folder, resolve it via search_folders. If you used n8n skills while preparing this workflow, pass their identifiers in skillsUsed. After creation, always tell the user which project — and folder, if any — the workflow landed in (see the targetProject and targetFolder fields in the response).

code.description: Full TypeScript/JavaScript workflow code using the n8n Workflow SDK. Must be validated first with validate_workflow. Max 300000 characters.

skillsUsed.description: IDs of n8n skills used to prepare this call, e.g. "workflow-builder". An optional plugin prefix is allowed, e.g. "n8n-skills:workflow-builder". Entries are normalized server-side (trimmed, lowercased, deduped); invalid identifiers are dropped.

name.description: Optional workflow name. If not provided, uses the name from the code.

description.description: Workflow description. Longer text is shortened to 255 chars before saving.

versionName.description: Short summary of this initial version, shown in the workflow's version history (e.g. "Initial Slack notification workflow"). Always provide it.

versionDescription.description: Longer description of what this version does, shown in the version history alongside the version name.

projectId.description: Project ID to create the workflow in. If the user named a project (e.g. 'in my Marketing project'), you MUST call search_projects first to resolve the name to an ID and pass it here — do not guess. If search_projects returns multiple partial matches with no exact match, ask the user to clarify before creating the workflow. Only omit this field when the user did not mention a project at all; in that case it defaults to the user's personal project.

folderId.description: Optional folder ID to create the workflow in. Requires projectId to be set. Use search_folders to find a folder by name within a project; when multiple folders match the name, ask the user which one they meant before creating.

create_workflow_from_code.name: create_workflow_from_code

workflowId.description: The ID of the created workflow

name.description: The name of the created workflow

nodeCount.description: The number of nodes in the workflow

url.description: The URL to open the workflow in n8n

autoAssignedCredentials.description: List of credentials that were automatically assigned to nodes

nodeName.description: The name of the node that had credentials auto-assigned

credentialName.description: The name of the credential that was auto-assigned

credentialType.description: The credential type that was auto-assigned

source.description: Where the credential came from: "user" for an existing user credential, "aiGateway" for a credential managed via Gateway credits.

id.description: The ID of the project the workflow was created in

name.description: The display name of the project the workflow was created in

type.description: Whether the workflow landed in a personal or team project

targetProject.description: The project the workflow was actually created in.

id.description: The ID of the folder the workflow was created in

name.description: The name of the folder the workflow was created in

targetFolder.description: The folder the workflow was created in. Absent when the workflow was created at the project root.

note.description: Additional notes about the workflow creation, such as any nodes that were skipped during credential auto-assignment.

skippedGroups.description: Node groups that were invalid and skipped instead of failing the whole creation. Repair them with update_workflow before you report the workflow as done.

hint.description: Actionable hint for recovering from the error. When present, follow the suggested action before retrying.

warnings.description: Validation warnings emitted while parsing the submitted code. Surface these to the user so they can correct the workflow.

code.description: The warning code identifying the type of warning

nodeName.description: The node that triggered the warning

parameterPath.description: The parameter path that triggered the warning

error.description: Error message explaining why the creation failed. Present only on failure.

errorCode.description: Machine-readable error code. Present only on failure.

list_n8n_gateway_services.name: list_n8n_gateway_services

available.description: True when Gateway credits are available for this instance. When false, the remaining fields are omitted.

credentialTypes.description: Credential type names Gateway credits can provide (e.g. "openAiApi").

supportedActions.description: Per-node allowlist keyed by node type, then resource (or `__operation_only__` for nodes without a resource dimension). Values are supported operation names.

minNodeTypeVersion.description: Minimum `typeVersion` per node type for Gateway credits coverage.

hiddenNodeProperties.description: Per-node property names hidden from the user when Gateway credits provide the credential.

rename_data_table_column.description: Rename a column in a data table.

dataTableId.description: The ID of the data table containing the column

projectId.description: The project ID the data table belongs to

columnId.description: The ID of the column to rename

name.description: The new column name

rename_data_table_column.name: rename_data_table_column

id.description: The unique identifier of the column

name.description: The name of the column

type.description: The data type of the column

add_data_table_rows.description: Insert rows into an existing data table. Each row is an object mapping column names to values. Use search_data_tables to find the data table ID first.

dataTableId.description: The ID of the data table to insert rows into

projectId.description: The project ID the data table belongs to

rows.description: Array of row objects to insert. Each object maps column names to values. Maximum 1000 rows per call.

add_data_table_rows.name: add_data_table_rows

get_data_table_rows.description: Read rows from a data table, with optional filtering, sorting and pagination. Use search_data_tables to find the data table ID and its columns first.

dataTableId.description: The ID of the data table to read rows from

projectId.description: The project ID the data table belongs to

type.description: How to combine the filters: all must match (and) or any may match (or)

columnName.description: Column to filter on. System columns 'id', 'createdAt' and 'updatedAt' are also allowed

condition.description: Comparison operator. 'like' (case-sensitive) and 'ilike' (case-insensitive) match substrings; include % wildcards for custom patterns. 'neq' also matches rows where the column is null

value.description: Value to compare against. For date columns, pass an ISO 8601 string. Pass null with eq/neq to match rows where the column is null / not null

filter.description: Filter conditions to select rows. Omit to return all rows

skip.description: Number of rows to skip, for paginating through large result sets

get_data_table_rows.name: get_data_table_rows

rows.description: Matching rows, mapping column names to values. Includes the system columns 'id', 'createdAt' and 'updatedAt'; dates are ISO 8601 strings

count.description: Total number of rows matching the filter, ignoring limit and skip

error.description: Error message if the read failed

mutate_agent.description: Apply one config, skill, task, or custom-tool mutation to an Agent draft. The operation fields sit directly on the operation object (no value wrapper), e.g. { "type": "config.patch", "patch": [...] }. Returns the next configHash for subsequent mutations.

baseConfigHash.description: Latest configHash returned by get_agent or a successful mutation

baseSkillHash.description: skillHashes[skillId] from get_agent; when set, the replace is rejected if the skill changed since

cronExpression.description: Standard five-field cron expression, for example "0 9 * * *"

anyOf.description: IANA timezone the cron is evaluated in, for example "Europe/London". Omit to use the instance timezone.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the cron is evaluated in, for example "Europe/London". Omit to use the instance timezone.

mutate_agent.name: mutate_agent

revert_agent.description: Restore an Agent draft from a published version, overwriting the draft config, skills, tasks, and custom tools. Does not publish. Inspect the version with get_agent first; the response returns the new configHash.

versionId.description: Published version to restore the draft from; defaults to the currently published version

revert_agent.name: revert_agent

update_agent_integration.description: Configure or disconnect a Slack, Telegram, or Linear conversation integration. This is the only way to manage integrations; config.replace and config.patch can't change them. Configuration never publishes the Agent. If the Agent is already published, connecting starts the channel immediately. Otherwise, the channel stays inactive until publish_agent is called. For Slack, connect without credentialId first: n8n returns the workspaces where it can create a Slack app for the Agent, or the steps the user must take in n8n. Then call again with managerCredentialId and workspaceId after the user confirms the workspace.

credentialId.description: Accessible credential for this integration. Required for disconnect and for non-Slack connect operations. Omit it to connect Slack through managed setup

managerCredentialId.description: Slack managed setup only: the managerCredentialId returned by a Slack connect call without credentialId

workspaceId.description: Slack managed setup only: the workspaceId returned by a Slack connect call without credentialId

settings.description: Integration settings; required for Telegram connect operations

replacesCredentialId.description: On connect, the credential of the same type this one takes over from. Swaps both in one operation instead of a separate disconnect

update_agent_integration.name: update_agent_integration

get_agent.description: Read an Agent draft, sidecar resources, runnable state, and configHash. Call before mutate_agent. Pass versionId to inspect a published version snapshot instead of the draft.

versionId.description: Read a published version snapshot instead of the draft, e.g. the activeVersionId. Snapshots are read-only, so the response has no configHash.

get_agent.name: get_agent

prepare_workflow_pin_data.description: Prepare test pin data for a workflow. Trigger nodes, nodes with credentials, and HTTP Request nodes need pin data. Logic nodes (Set, If, Code, etc.) and credential-free I/O nodes (Execute Command, file read/write) execute normally without pin data. Returns JSON Schemas describing the expected output shape for each node that needs pin data — schemas are derived from past execution output shapes or node type definitions. No actual user data is returned. You should generate realistic sample data for the schemas, use empty defaults for nodes without schema, merge everything into a single pinData object, and pass it to test_workflow.

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow to generate test pin data for

prepare_workflow_pin_data.name: prepare_workflow_pin_data

nodeSchemasToGenerate.description: Nodes that need pin data generated by you. Keys are node names, values are JSON Schema objects describing the expected output shape. Schemas may come from node type definitions or inferred from past execution output shapes. Generate realistic sample data matching each schema, wrap each item as {"json": {...}}, and collect into a pinData object to pass to test_workflow.

nodesWithoutSchema.description: Node names that need pin data but have no output schema. Generate a single item [{"json": {}}] for each, and merge into pinData before passing to test_workflow.

nodesSkipped.description: Nodes that do not need pin data and will execute normally during the test (e.g. Set, If, Code, Merge).

withSchemaFromExecution.description: Number of nodes with schemas inferred from last successful execution output

withSchemaFromDefinition.description: Number of nodes with schemas from node type definitions

withoutSchema.description: Number of nodes with no data or schema — use empty defaults

skipped.description: Number of nodes that will execute normally (no pin data needed)

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow to publish

versionId.description: Optional version ID to publish. If not provided, publishes the current draft version.

After installing, call get_node_types for the returned node types before writing workflow code.

install_community_node.name: install_community_node

alreadyInstalled.description: True when the node was already available, so nothing was installed. Not an error: carry on and use the node.

nodeTypes.description: Node types the package registered, now usable in workflow code. Call get_node_types on these before writing the workflow — the installed definition is authoritative.

credentialTypes.description: Credential types the installed nodes require. These only exist now that the package is installed, so the user must create one in n8n before the workflow can run. Tell them which.

get_workflow_best_practices.description: Required planning step when building a workflow, and only then. Get best-practices guidance (recommended nodes, patterns, and common pitfalls) for a specific workflow technique before searching for nodes or writing code. Call once per relevant technique. Use technique="list" first if unsure which techniques apply.

technique.description: Workflow technique key to fetch best-practices guidance for. Pass "list" to discover all available techniques. One of: list, scheduling, chatbot, form_input, scraping_and_research, monitoring, enrichment, triage, content_generation, document_processing, data_extraction, data_analysis, data_transformation, data_persistence, notification, knowledge_base, human_in_the_loop, web_app.

get_workflow_best_practices.name: get_workflow_best_practices

technique.description: The requested technique key, or "list" when listing all available techniques.

documentation.description: Best-practices documentation for the requested technique, when one with documentation was requested.

availableTechniques.description: All available techniques, returned when "list" was requested.

get_workflow_execution.description: Get workflow execution details by execution ID and workflow ID. By default returns metadata only. Set includeData to true to include node execution data, optionally filtered by nodeNames and truncated by truncateData.

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow the execution belongs to

executionId.description: The ID of the execution to retrieve

includeData.description: Whether to include the full execution result data. Defaults to false (metadata only). Set to true to include node inputs/outputs. Use `false` to quickly check execution status

nodeNames.description: When includeData is true, return data only for these node names. If omitted, data for all nodes is included.

truncateData.description: When includeData is true, limit the number of data items returned per node output to this value. If omitted, all items are returned.

get_workflow_execution.name: get_workflow_execution

execution.description: Execution metadata, or null if an error occurred

data.description: Execution result data (only present when includeData is true)

error.description: Error message if the request failed

execute_workflow.description: Execute a workflow by ID. Returns the execution ID immediately without waiting for completion. Before executing always ensure you know the input schema by first using the get_workflow_details tool and consulting workflow description; pass detailLevel 'execution' to that tool when running the workflow is all you need, since the full graph is not required here.

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow to execute

executionMode.description: Required execution intent. Use "manual" for testing or validating the current workflow, including tests against live external services. Use "production" only when intentionally running the published workflow as a live execution.

triggerNodeName.description: Name of the trigger node to execute. Required when providing inputs. If omitted, the workflow must have exactly one trigger that does not require inputs (Schedule Trigger, or Manual Trigger in manual mode). Use get_workflow_details to see available trigger names.

inputs.description: Trigger payload. Required for webhook, chat, and form triggers. Must be omitted for schedule and manual triggers. Use get_workflow_details to see the expected payload for each trigger.

execute_workflow.name: execute_workflow

error.description: Error message if the execution failed

gatewayCredits.description: Present when Gateway credits are available. Candidate coverage — cross-reference against the search results, but call list_n8n_gateway_services for exact eligibility (supported actions, min versions, hidden properties).

search_workflows.description: Search for workflows with optional filters. Returns a preview of each workflow. Where workflows are organised into folders, narrow the search with folderId instead of scanning everything: reuse a parentFolderId from an earlier result, or resolve a folder name with search_folders when that tool is available.

tags.description: Filter by tag names (AND semantics — workflow must have all).

sortBy.description: Sort order for results (default: updatedAt:desc). Use updatedAt:desc to find the most recently edited workflows first.

folderId.description: Filter by folder. Pass a parentFolderId from an earlier result to find a workflow's siblings, or — when search_folders is available — use it to resolve a folder name to an id first. Pass "0" for workflows that sit at the project root rather than in a folder.

includeSubfolders.description: Whether a folderId search also covers that folder's subfolders (default: true). Set false to match only workflows directly inside the folder. Ignored when folderId is "0", which always matches the project root only.

search_workflows.name: search_workflows

modelsByDifficulty.description: Optional inline sub-agent model mappings by task difficulty. Missing mappings fall back to the parent agent model.

search_projects.description: Search for projects accessible to the current user. Call this whenever the user names a project — pass the name as the query, then use the resolved ID with tools that take a projectId. Results are ranked with exact case-insensitive name matches first. If no exact match is found but multiple partials are returned, the response includes a `hint` field telling you to clarify with the user before acting; follow it instead of guessing. The response also includes `teamProjectsEnabled` — when false, team projects are not licensed on this instance, so default to creating in the caller's personal project unless the user explicitly picks one of the returned accessible projects.

query.description: Filter projects by name (case-insensitive partial match). Pass the exact project name the user mentioned — results are ranked with exact case-insensitive matches first, then partial matches.

type.description: Filter by project type. 'team' for shared team projects, 'personal' for personal projects.

search_projects.name: search_projects

data.description: List of projects matching the query, sorted with exact case-insensitive matches first.

id.description: The unique identifier of the project

name.description: The name of the project

matchType.description: Whether this project's name matches the query exactly (case-insensitive) or only partially. Only present when a query was provided.

teamProjectsEnabled.description: Whether team projects are licensed on this n8n instance. When false, default to omitting projectId on create_workflow_from_code so the workflow lands in the caller's personal project, unless the user explicitly picked one of the returned accessible projects (legacy team projects can still appear here after a license downgrade). Omitted on error responses.

hint.description: Guidance for picking a result. Present when the match is ambiguous — for example when no exact match was found but multiple partials were returned, or when team projects are not licensed on this instance. When present, follow it before calling create_workflow_from_code.

update_workflow.description: Atomically update an existing workflow with operation objects. Edits nodes/connections and also workflow-level settings via setWorkflowSettings — including the error workflow that runs automatically on failure to send alerts (e.g. when a user asks to "add error handling" or "notify me if this breaks"). Pass skillsUsed if n8n skills were used. Node-group operations (setNodeGroups, addNodeGroup, removeNodeGroup, updateNodeGroup) are the one exception to "atomically": an invalid one is skipped and reported in skippedOperations instead of aborting the whole update. Separately, if other edits in the batch make an existing group invalid, that group is removed and reported in removedGroups.

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow to update.

skillsUsed.description: IDs of n8n skills used to prepare this call, e.g. "workflow-builder". An optional plugin prefix is allowed, e.g. "n8n-skills:workflow-builder". Entries are normalized server-side (trimmed, lowercased, deduped); invalid identifiers are dropped.

operations.description: Ordered operations to apply atomically (max 100). If any op fails, nothing is saved — except node-group operations (setNodeGroups, addNodeGroup, removeNodeGroup, updateNodeGroup): an invalid one is skipped and reported in skippedOperations, while the rest of the batch still saves. An existing group that these ops leave invalid is removed and reported in removedGroups.

name.description: Unique node name.

sourceIndex.description: For connection ops; which output of the source node the connection starts from. Default 0, the first output. Use it to wire a branch: on an If node the false branch is index 1, and onError "continueErrorOutput" appends an error output after the regular ones (index 1 on a single-output node such as HTTP Request, index 2 on an If node). This is the only field that selects an output.

targetIndex.description: For connection ops; which input of the target node the connection ends at. Default 0.

onError.description: Error behavior. "continueErrorOutput" appends an error output after the node's regular outputs — index 1 on a single-output node such as HTTP Request. Wire that branch with an addConnection operation whose sourceIndex is that index.

errorWorkflow.description: ID of a SEPARATE workflow to run whenever THIS workflow fails — the common best-practice way to send failure alerts (email, Slack, etc.) or log errors via a shared, reusable handler. The referenced workflow must contain an Error Trigger node; find its ID with search_workflows. Pass "DEFAULT" to clear it. Must be a plain ID — this setting is never evaluated, so an expression would be stored as a literal ID and the handler would never run. There are two ways to handle failures: (a) a dedicated/shared error workflow set here, or (b) an Error Trigger node placed directly inside THIS workflow (n8n fires it automatically on failure, no setting needed). When the user asks for error handling, ask which pattern they prefer before choosing. When errorWorkflow is set, it takes precedence over a same-workflow Error Trigger for the failing run. Failure handling fires for production executions only, not manual/test runs. Distinct from per-node onError/retry (setNodeSettings).

timezone.description: IANA timezone used by Schedule Triggers and date/time operations, e.g. "America/New_York". Pass "DEFAULT" to inherit the instance timezone.

executionOrder.description: Node execution order. "v1" is the default for new workflows; "v0" is legacy.

saveExecutionProgress.description: Save execution data after each node finishes. Allows resuming/inspecting partial runs at the cost of speed.

saveManualExecutions.description: Whether manual (test) executions are saved to the execution list.

saveDataErrorExecution.description: Whether to store execution data for failed runs.

saveDataSuccessExecution.description: Whether to store execution data for successful runs.

executionTimeout.description: Maximum execution time in seconds before a run is stopped. Use a positive number of seconds (not exceeding the instance maximum, enforced server-side), or -1 for unlimited (no timeout).

timeSavedPerExecution.description: Estimated time saved per execution, in minutes (used for insights/reporting).

callerPolicy.description: Which workflows may call this one via the Execute Sub-workflow node. Defaults to "workflowsFromSameOwner".

callerIds.description: Comma-separated workflow IDs allowed to call this workflow (only used with callerPolicy "workflowsFromAList").

name.description: For setWorkflowMetadata (workflow name) or addNodeGroup (group name).

nodeGroups.description: For setNodeGroups. Replaces all node groups; pass [] to clear. Group members are node names, not ids.

nodeNames.description: For addNodeGroup / updateNodeGroup; group member node names.

id.description: For addNodeGroup; group id, generated if omitted.

items.description: Workflow update operation. Provide fields matching type.

versionName.description: Short summary of what this update changes, shown in the workflow's version history (e.g. "Added Slack notification after HTTP request"). Always provide it.

versionDescription.description: Longer description of what changed and why, shown in the version history alongside the version name.

update_workflow.name: update_workflow

appliedOperations.description: Number of submitted operations that were applied. See skippedOperations for any that were not.

autoAssignedCredentials.description: Credentials auto-assigned to nodes that were added in this update.

validationWarnings.description: Graph and JSON validation warnings on the resulting workflow. Warnings marked preExisting (also tagged [pre-existing] in the message) were already present before this update; only self-correct the rest on the next call.

preExisting.description: True when the same warning already existed before this update — it was not caused by these operations.

skippedOperations.description: Submitted group operations that did not take effect: either invalid, or their group broke the group rules.

removedGroups.description: Existing groups this update made invalid and removed. Repair them before you report the workflow as done.

settings.description: Resulting workflow-level settings after the update. Present only when a setWorkflowSettings operation ran. Reflects server-side cleanup (e.g. "DEFAULT" values are removed).

error.description: Error message explaining why the update failed. Present only on failure.

get_node_types.description: Get TypeScript type definitions for n8n nodes. Returns exact parameter names and structures. MUST be called before writing workflow code or configuring node-backed tools — guessing parameter names creates invalid configurations. Pass nodeIds as an array of objects like { nodeId: "n8n-nodes-base.gmail" }. Include discriminators (resource/operation/mode) from search_nodes results.

nodeIds.description: Node type requests to get definitions for. Always pass an array of objects, even for a single node. Include discriminators from search_nodes results when available.

get_node_types.name: get_node_types

definitions.description: TypeScript type definitions for the requested nodes

credentialTypes.description: Credential types Gateway credits can provide.

nodes.description: Node types Gateway credits may cover. Prefer these when the user has not specified an integration. Candidate coverage only — exact eligibility also depends on the node action, minimum type version, and hidden properties.

gatewayCredits.description: Present when Gateway credits are available. Candidate coverage — cross-reference against the returned node types, but call list_n8n_gateway_services for exact eligibility (supported actions, min versions, hidden properties).

explore_node_resources.description: Resolve the real values behind a node's resource locator or load-options dropdown (e.g. Slack channels, Google Sheets tabs, OpenAI models). Use this after get_node_types so you ground RLC and load-options parameters in real IDs instead of inventing them. Requires a credential ID from list_credentials — the call runs as the current user with that credential.

nodeType.description: Fully-qualified node type ID from search_nodes / get_node_types, e.g. "n8n-nodes-base.slack".

version.description: Node version, e.g. 4.7. Must match a version returned by search_nodes.

methodName.description: The exact method name from the node's `@searchListMethod` or `@loadOptionsMethod` annotation in the type definition. Call get_node_types first to read the real method name. Do not invent or guess.

credentialType.description: Credential type key for the node, e.g. "slackApi" or "googleSheetsOAuth2Api".

credentialId.description: ID of a credential the user can access, obtained from list_credentials.

filter.description: Optional search/filter text to narrow results.

paginationToken.description: Pagination token from a previous call to fetch the next page (listSearch only).

currentNodeParameters.description: Current node parameters for dependent lookups. Some methods require prior selections — e.g. listing sheets within a spreadsheet needs `{ documentId: { __rl: true, mode: "id", value: "<spreadsheetId>" } }`. Check the type definition's displayOptions to know which parameters a method depends on.

test_workflow.description: Test a workflow using pin data to bypass external services. Trigger nodes, nodes with credentials, and HTTP Request nodes are pinned (use simulated data). Other nodes (Set, If, Code, etc.) execute normally — including credential-free I/O nodes like Execute Command or file read/write nodes. Use prepare_workflow_pin_data to generate the pin data first.

workflowId.description: The ID of the workflow to test

pinData.description: Pin data for all workflow nodes. Use the prepare_workflow_pin_data tool to generate this. Keys are node names, values are arrays of items. Each item MUST be wrapped in a "json" property, e.g. [{"json": {"id": "123", "name": "test"}}]. Do NOT pass flat objects like [{"id": "123"}].

triggerNodeName.description: Optional name of the trigger node to start execution from. Useful for workflows with multiple triggers. Defaults to the first trigger node found.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds before the test execution is interrupted. Defaults to 300 seconds. Increase this to test workflows that take longer to run.

test_workflow.name: test_workflow

status.description: The status of the test execution

error.description: Error message if the execution failed

validate_node_config.description: Validate a node's config the moment you write it — before assembling create_workflow_from_code or calling update_workflow. Read-only and needs no existing workflow, so use it freely while composing. Unlike the write tools (which validate only as they mutate), this returns isolated per-node, per-parameter errors with no graph noise, and can check several candidate configs in one call so you wire only the one that passes. For langchain tool subnodes (nodes wired via ai_tool), set isToolNode: true so the schema evaluates the correct displayOptions branch. Schema-level only — for connections, required inputs, triggers, and credentials use validate_workflow.

nodes.description: One or more node configurations to validate independently.

name.description: Optional node name. Echoed back in the result so callers can correlate.

parameters.description: Node parameters object — same shape as workflow JSON.

subnodes.description: Optional subnode config for AI parent nodes (e.g. langchain agent): `{ model, memory, tools: [...] }` of `{ type, version }` refs.

isToolNode.description: Set to true when validating a node that is wired as an AI tool subnode (ai_tool connection). Adjusts which displayOptions branch is evaluated.

validate_node_config.name: validate_node_config

valid.description: True when every node is valid.

results.description: Per-node validation results, in input order.

index.description: Position of this node in the input array.

name.description: Echo of the input name, if provided.

type.description: Echo of the input node type.

valid.description: Whether this node config is valid.

errors.description: Validation errors for this node (omitted when valid).

error.description: Top-level error message when validation could not run at all (e.g. internal failure loading the schema). Omitted on success.

validate_workflow.description: Validate n8n Workflow SDK code. Required before creating or updating workflows from code. If you have not already read get_workflow_sdk_reference, call that first; guessing SDK syntax commonly creates invalid workflows.

code.description: Full TypeScript/JavaScript workflow code using the n8n Workflow SDK. Must include the workflow export. Max 300000 characters.

validate_workflow.name: validate_workflow

valid.description: Whether the workflow code is valid

nodeCount.description: The number of nodes in the workflow (if valid)

code.description: The warning code identifying the type of warning

nodeName.description: The node that triggered the warning

parameterPath.description: The parameter path that triggered the warning

hint.description: Actionable hint for recovering from the error. When present, follow the suggested action before retrying.

list_agent_versions.description: List the publish history of an Agent, newest first. Pass a versionId to get_agent to inspect a version before revert_agent or publish_agent.
